name: WA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Emily Randall with large fundraising edge
model.rationale: The district's D+10 lean, Randall's incumbency and roughly 40-to-1 fundraising advantage over Teresa Fox, and Polymarket pricing near 94% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold with no contrary evidence on record.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Randall would be the first signal the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Emily Randall, a Democratic incumbent, seeks a second term in a western Washington district that leans Democratic by about ten points. She has raised nearly $1.2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Teresa Fox has raised under $30,000 with no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Randall roughly a 94% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money gap, and market pricing all align on a comfortable Democratic hold, with an expected margin of about 21 points and modest uncertainty given the absence of direct polling.
